content.text:
Yes, one thing. It comes from `files.csv` and the design table, not from the data contents.

**Sequencing lane is partly confounded with condition.** Each sample sits on a single lane:

| Condition | Samples (lane) |
|---|---|
| control | S1 (L002), S2 (L001), S3 (L002) |
| treated | S4 (L001), S5 (L001), S6 (L002) |

Control is mostly L002 and treated is mostly L001. The imbalance is 2:1 in opposite directions. If lane or run carries a technical effect, part of it would load onto the treated-versus-control contrast. Lanes on one flowcell usually differ little. I can't tell from the registered files whether these lanes share a flowcell or run, so I can't say how much this matters.

A few related points:
- **No batch term in the design.** `rnaseq_bulk_design.csv` has only `sample_id,condition,group,replicate`. Lane isn't a design column, so the model formula can't adjust for it unless you add it. Lane is also not a replicate structure. Each sample has exactly one lane, so there are no technical replicates to merge.
- **Small n.** There are 3 samples per group. That passes the stage 01 check (at least 2 per group), but power is limited and the dispersion estimates will be noisy.
- **`condition` and `group` are identical.** They carry the same information, so only one can go into the formula. `replicate` (1–3) is just a within-group index, not a pairing or blocking variable. Unless S1 and S4 are really the same donor or animal, treat this as an unpaired comparison.

`00_data/rnaseq_bulk/raw/` also had `README_runsheet.txt`, which was excluded as non-FASTQ. I haven't read it, because stage 00's scope forbids it. If you want to know whether the lanes correspond to different runs, it may say.

If lane is a concern, you could add a column to the design before approving the samplesheet. That's your edit to make, and the formula is chosen at stage 02. Otherwise the samplesheet is ready for your approval as it stands.
